introduction-the-needle-in-the-haystack-.core: A latency histogram shows p99 jumped to 2 s, but which requests were slow? Metrics are aggregates with no request identity, and searching millions of traces for the right one is slow. Exemplars bridge the gap: they attach a sample trace ID to specific metric values, so you can click a dot on the latency graph and open a real trace that produced that value.

first_principles.problem: Engineers see a p99 spike and spend 30 minutes searching the trace store for an example slow request.

analogy.title: A survey statistic with a quoted respondent
analogy.story: '30% unhappy' plus a link to an actual unhappy customer's comment.
analogy.breaks: Survey quotes are curated; exemplars are picked automatically.

example.title: Spike to trace
flow: p99 latency panel shows spike at 14:05

check.q: What does an exemplar add to a metric sample?
check.a: A reference (usually a trace ID) to a specific request that contributed to that value.

what-is-an-exemplar.core: An exemplar is a small record attached to a metric observation: the value (for example 1.92 s), a timestamp, and labels such as trace_id and span_id. For histograms, each bucket can carry its most recent exemplar. The metrics backend stores a limited number per series, so exemplars are a sample, not a complete index, but enough to give a real example for any part of the distribution.

first_principles.problem: An engineer assumes exemplars index every request and is confused when only a few appear.
derivation: Use as **entry points**, not full search.

analogy.title: A sample product in each display case
analogy.story: Each shelf (bucket) shows one example item; the warehouse (trace store) holds everything.
analogy.breaks: Display items are fixed; exemplars update constantly.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Bucket le=2.5 carries an example 1.92 s request.

check.q: Are exemplars a complete index of all requests?
check.a: No, they're a bounded sample, typically the latest example per bucket, used as entry points into traces.

the-openmetrics-standard.core: Exemplars require the OpenMetrics exposition format (application/openmetrics-text), which extends Prometheus text format with exemplar syntax after a #, along with stricter typing, _created timestamps and a mandatory EOF. Prometheus must scrape with OpenMetrics negotiation and run with --enable-feature=exemplar-storage, and OTLP carries exemplars natively for push pipelines. Remote-write backends such as Mimir need exemplar ingestion enabled too.

first_principles.problem: Exemplars are instrumented in code but never appear, because Prometheus scrapes the classic text format.
derivation: Enable exemplars in **remote write** and backend.

analogy.title: A postal form with an optional attachment box
analogy.story: If the post office uses the old form without the box, attachments are discarded.
analogy.breaks: Forms are visible; content negotiation failures are silent.

code.text:
prometheus --enable-feature=exemplar-storage --storage.exemplars.exemplars-limit=100000
# prometheus.yml remote_write: [{ url: ..., send_exemplars: true }]
curl -s 'localhost:9090/api/v1/query_exemplars?query=http_request_duration_seconds_bucket&start=now-1h&end=now' | jq '.data[0].exemplars[0]'

check.q: Why might instrumented exemplars not show up in Prometheus?
check.a: It's scraping the classic text format or exemplar-storage isn't enabled, so exemplars are dropped.

the-instrumentation-layer-connecting-tra.core: To create exemplars, the code recording a metric must know the current trace context. With OpenTelemetry SDKs, histogram and counter recordings inside an active span attach exemplars automatically when exemplar filters allow it (by default, sampled traces only). With prometheus_client you pass exemplar={'trace_id': ...}. Only attach exemplars from sampled traces; otherwise the link leads to a trace that was never stored.

first_principles.problem: Exemplars link to trace IDs that return 'trace not found' because those traces weren't sampled.
truths: Metrics and spans must share context.
Unsampled traces don't exist in storage.

analogy.title: Citing a reference only if it's in the library
analogy.story: A footnote is useless if it points to a book the library never kept.
analogy.breaks: Libraries rarely discard books; samplers discard most traces.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Exemplars only point to stored traces.

code.text:
from opentelemetry import trace
ctx = trace.get_current_span().get_span_context()
exemplar = {"trace_id": format(ctx.trace_id, "032x")} if ctx.trace_flags.sampled else None
LATENCY.labels(route="/checkout").observe(duration, exemplar=exemplar)

check.q: Why should exemplars only be attached for sampled traces?
check.a: Unsampled traces aren't stored, so the exemplar's link would lead to a missing trace.

the-user-experience-in-grafana.core: In Grafana, enable 'Exemplars' on a Prometheus query and the time series panel overlays dots at exemplar values. Hovering shows the trace ID and labels, and clicking opens the trace in Tempo or Jaeger via the datasource's exemplar link configuration (internal link with a trace_id label mapping). Dots on a latency spike lead straight to representative slow requests.

first_principles.problem: Exemplars exist in Prometheus, but the dashboard shows nothing clickable.
truths: Display must be enabled per query.
derivation: Configure **exemplar trace ID destination** in Prometheus datasource.

analogy.title: Pins on a map that open photos
analogy.story: Each pin marks where something happened; tap it to see the picture.
analogy.breaks: Map pins are permanent; exemplars age out.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Click a dot → Tempo trace opens.

code.text:
datasources:
  - name: Prometheus
    type: prometheus
    url: http://prometheus:9090
    jsonData:
      exemplarTraceIdDestinations:
        - name: trace_id
          datasourceUid: tempo

check.q: What Grafana setting makes exemplar dots clickable to a trace?
check.a: The Prometheus datasource's exemplar trace ID destinations, mapping the trace_id label to a tracing datasource.

exemplars-in-the-broader-observability-p.core: Exemplars are one link in a connected observability graph: metrics go to traces via exemplars, traces to logs via trace_id, traces to profiles via span profiles, and logs to metrics via derived metrics. Consistent context (trace IDs, service names, resource attributes) is what makes those jumps possible. The goal is a seamless investigation path from 'something's wrong' to 'this line of code'.

first_principles.problem: A team has metrics, logs, traces and profiles in separate tools with no links between them.

analogy.title: Hyperlinked encyclopedia articles
analogy.story: Each article links to related ones, so you can follow a topic from overview to detail.
analogy.breaks: Encyclopedias are curated; links depend on instrumentation consistency.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Alert to root cause without manual searching.

check.q: What makes it possible to pivot between metrics, traces, logs and profiles?
check.a: Shared context such as trace IDs and consistent resource attributes (service, version) present in every signal.
